source.title: Experimental increase in predation risk causes a cascading stress response in free-ranging snowshoe hares

confidence_rationale: Directly on-point ecological field experiment: predation risk (the closest wild analogue to REE's num_hazards / hazard_food_attraction manipulation) was manipulated in free-ranging animals and physiological stress measures rose in a graded, measurable way with the manipulation. This is real evidence that a physiological stress signal CAN and DOES faithfully track predation-risk intensity in a directly analogous chronic/ecological context, weakening any strong prior that ecological tracking is implausible. But the paper also found that whole-organism condition indices were UNAFFECTED despite the physiological stress rise, indicating compensation/buffering -- the physiological readout moved while the organism's overall state did not degrade correspondingly, which complicates a naive 'the physiological signal = the true suffering level' reading and is why this is scored mixed rather than a clean support.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Experimentally increasing predation risk (simulated predator chases) in free-ranging snowshoe hares over two summers produced a graded, statistically robust physiological stress cascade relative to controls: 25.8% higher free plasma cortisol, 15.9% lower cortisol-binding capacity, a greater neutrophil:lymphocyte skew, and a 10.4% increase in glucose. Despite this, two independent condition indices were unaffected by risk exposure across the study period, which the authors attribute to compensatory foraging and/or metabolic adjustment.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the most directly analogous real-world manipulation to REE's V3-EXQ-857/857a design: predation-risk intensity is manipulated in the wild and a physiological harm/stress readout is measured for a graded response. The headline finding -- physiological stress DOES scale measurably with predation-risk manipulation in a genuinely ecological, chronic-exposure setting -- is evidence that the 'faithful ecological tracking' reading of Q-086 is not merely a hopeful just-so story; graded tracking of hazard intensity by a physiological signal is a real, demonstrated phenomenon in exactly this kind of manipulation. The unaffected condition indices are the more interesting wrinkle for REE: they show that a rising physiological/affective readout can coexist with the organism successfully buffering the ecological consequences of that risk -- i.e. the SIGNAL rising is not the same claim as the organism's true fitness-relevant state degrading correspondingly. This maps onto a live design question for z_harm_a: is it meant to track proximate physiological/affective load (which this paper shows CAN scale even under compensation), or downstream functional consequence (which this paper shows can remain flat even while the proximate signal rises)? Q-086's framing conflates these two readings, and this paper is direct evidence they can dissociate.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a single species (Lepus americanus), two field seasons, comparing risk-augmented vs control groups rather than a graded dose-response curve across multiple hazard-intensity levels (REE's manipulation compares two discrete environment configurations, closer in spirit but still not a multi-point curve). The physiological measures (plasma cortisol, cortisol-binding capacity, neutrophil:lymphocyte ratio, glucose) are endocrine/immune, not neural/representational, so this speaks to whether ecological tracking of hazard intensity is physiologically plausible in principle, not to whether REE's specific z_harm_a/z_harm_s architecture implements it correctly. Wild mammal predation-risk physiology to an artificial RL agent's internal harm signal is a substantial domain transfer.
mapping.source_context: Free-ranging snowshoe hares (Lepus americanus) in the wild, monitored via intensive radio-telemetry across two consecutive summers; predation risk experimentally increased using a model predator to simulate natural chases; physiological assays for stress hormones, immune markers, and metabolic indices; condition indices tracked intra-annually.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high: a genuine field experiment (not observational) with intensive telemetry monitoring, published in a strong ecology journal, directly manipulating the variable of interest (predation risk) rather than inferring it. Mapping fidelity moderate: predation-risk manipulation in the wild is the closest real-world analogue to REE's num_hazards/hazard_food_attraction environment manipulation, but the readouts (endocrine/immune) are a different modality from REE's internal scalar affective signal. Transfer risk moderate: wild mammal to artificial agent is a real gap, but the ecological logic (does a physiological signal track manipulated risk) transfers reasonably well as a existence-proof-level argument.
